title: Cognitive Exhaust Fumes, or: Read-Only AI Is Underrated — Šimon Podhajský, Head of AI, Waypoint

summary: Šimon Podhajský, Head of AI at Waypoint, challenges the industry's agent-first orthodoxy by presenting a personal AI system constrained to read-only access across six data sources. He introduces the metaphor of "cognitive exhaust fumes"—digital activity byproducts that, like car exhaust, can be analyzed to diagnose the engine of cognition. The system architecture has three zones: read-only sources, a workspace for analysis, and a separate output vault (Obsidian, though any system works). Everything runs through Claude with Python scripts that pull structured outputs from the Anthropic API. He demonstrates two applications: a weekly reflection that synthesizes tensions, commitments, and notable moments from exhaust data, and a cross-source query that recommends people in his network to discuss recent reading with, combining browser history, CRM contacts, and other sources. The core argument is about trust asymmetry: read-only errors have zero downside while write errors are unbounded, operating in high-stakes personal environments. Beyond safety, read-only produces better analysis because writing back contaminates the exhaust with human-AI hybrid patterns. He frames observers and agents as different product categories, rejecting the industry framing of read-only as a limitation to graduate from. He concludes with a paranoid security review, acknowledging the mosaic effect risk and that the system does not fully break Simon Willison's lethal triquetra due to shell access and external API calls. He explicitly disclaims that the system is not secure but rather that he has examined and consciously accepted specific risks.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.
temporalContext: Transcript claims reflect the publication date; linked external context was checked at the run's research date.
takeaways: Read-only AI is a different product category from agents, not a stepping stone toward them
Trust asymmetry is fundamental: read errors have zero downside, write errors are unbounded
Cross-source pattern detection across disconnected data sources surfaces insights no single tool can provide
"Cognitive exhaust fumes"—digital byproducts of cognition—can be analyzed to diagnose your thinking patterns
Writing back to data sources contaminates the exhaust, making it impossible to distinguish your patterns from AI-influenced ones
The system is explicitly not secure; the speaker has examined risks and chosen which to accept rather than remaining ignorant
The mosaic effect makes cross-referenced personal data a devastating target even as it makes the system useful
The observer model produces more value per interaction than the agent model for personal intelligence
Three top use cases: intention-action gaps, attention drift, and relationship decay
Understand why read-only constraints produce better analytical architecture than agent-first approaches for personal AI

sections.title: Introduction and Concept
sections.summary: Šimon introduces a personal AI system that knows you but won't act on your behalf, contrasting it with agent-obsessed personal AI space. He defines cognitive exhaust fumes as digital activity byproducts of cognition.

sections.title: System Architecture
sections.summary: Three-zone architecture: read-only sources, workspace for analysis, and separate output vault. Six sources, no write permissions. Outputs land in Obsidian but could be any system.

sections.title: Weekly Reflection Demo
sections.summary: Demonstrates a Claude skill that runs a Python script to pull data from six read-only sources, sends structured prompts to Anthropic API, and produces a markdown reflection covering themes, tensions, commitments, notable moments, and reflection questions. Emphasizes it is a reflection on thinking, not a productivity report.

sections.title: Cross-Source Network Query Demo
sections.summary: Demonstrates asking AI who in his network he should discuss recent reading with. System queries Vivaldi SQLite for most-read articles and Clay CRM for interested contacts, maps people to articles. Notes token consumption is significant and Clay MCP is slow.

sections.title: Why Read-Only: Trust Asymmetry and Contamination
sections.summary: Argues read-only is necessary because downside of read errors is zero while write errors are unbounded in high-stakes personal environments. Writing back contaminates exhaust fumes, making patterns indistinguishable. Observer produces more value than agent. Read-only is a different product category, not a limitation to graduate from.

sections.title: Security Paranoia: Mosaic Effect and Lethal Triquetra
sections.summary: Acknowledges mosaic effect risk where cross-referencing creates a devastating target. Discusses Simon Willison's lethal triquetra: system removes natural exfiltration channels but shell access still enables external communication. Explicitly disclaims security, stating he has examined risks and chosen which to accept. Concludes that digital exhaust is the most underused dataset you own.

demonstrations: Weekly reflection skill: Python script pulls data from six read-only sources, sends structured prompts to Anthropic API, generates a markdown reflection document covering themes, tensions, commitments, notable moments, and reflection questions

Cross-source network query: Claude skill queries Vivaldi SQLite browser database for most-read articles and Clay CRM for contacts interested in those topics, maps people to articles for discussion recommendations
limitations: System is not fireproof or secure; data sent to Anthropic over a mostly open network
Does not fully break the lethal triquetra due to shell access enabling external communication
More information exposed than strictly required
Clay MCP is slow, described as the weakest part
Cross-source queries consume significant context window tokens
Observer effect still changes behavior, though mediated by the human rather than automated
quantitativeClaims: Agent saves 30 seconds on a weather check; observer reveals avoiding most important project for 2 weeks
Cross-source query uses significant context window tokens, manageable within 1 million context window of Claude 4.6
Clay MCP takes a long time to run
